cl_lsd_vs_psilocybin.q: LSD or mushrooms: what's actually different?
cl_lsd_vs_psilocybin.short: Mostly how long it lasts: about 9 to 11 hours for LSD, 6 to 7 for psilocybin, the drug in mushrooms. Otherwise 28 lab volunteers rated the trips alike on most measures.
cl_lsd_vs_psilocybin.but: Finding no difference in 28 people doesn't prove there is none. And most could tell which drug they'd had.
how: 28 healthy adults each had five hospital days, at least 10 days apart. They got a dummy, two amounts of LSD and two of psilocybin, in random order, not told which.
LSD lasted longer at both amounts. It also began a bit sooner, which the authors put down to it being a liquid, not a capsule.

The higher psilocybin amount raised blood pressure and body temperature a little more; the higher LSD amount raised heart rate more. On a checklist, 13 to 18 of the 28 had a headache in the first 12 hours after the drugs, against 8 on the dummy. Nobody had a serious problem.
People named the right drug after 71 to 86 in 100 sessions, and the dummy after every session, which may have shaped their ratings. It used pure psilocybin in capsules, not mushrooms.
cl_lsd_vs_psilocybin.rate: One careful lab study of 28 people, who took both drugs in random order. But most could tell which drug they had, and 'alike' only means no clear difference was found.

cl_mix_mdma_lsd.q: What if I take LSD and MDMA at the same time?
cl_mix_mdma_lsd.short: Blood pressure and heart rate went higher than on LSD alone, and bad feelings weren't clearly eased. In a lab study of 24 people, top blood pressure was 13 points higher.
cl_mix_mdma_lsd.but: Healthy people took one amount of each, in a calm hospital room. Nothing serious happened, but 24 people can't show rare dangers.
how: 24 healthy adults each had four hospital days, at least 10 days apart. They got LSD, MDMA, both at once, or a dummy, in random order and without being told which.

With both, top blood pressure averaged 150, against 137 on LSD alone and 148 on MDMA alone; heart rate 100 beats a minute, against 92 and 95. Body temperature was not clearly higher than on LSD alone.

Bad-feeling, fear and complaint scores were not clearly lower than on LSD alone, and more people had trembling, restless legs or teeth grinding. Nausea in the first 12 hours: 11 of 24 with both, 14 on MDMA alone, 7 on LSD alone, 4 on the dummy. Nobody had a serious problem.

The two drugs changed each other's blood levels: more LSD stayed in the blood for longer, while MDMA peaked lower and later. The effects lasted about an hour and a half longer than on LSD alone, and the longest lasted 21 hours.
cl_mix_mdma_lsd.rate: One careful lab study of 24 healthy people, with one amount of each drug taken together. The blood pressure results are clear; the rest rests on people's own ratings, and rare dangers can't show up in so few.

cl_can_strain_labels.q: Do indica and sativa labels tell you what's in your weed?
cl_can_strain_labels.short: Mostly not. In 41,201 lab-tested US weed samples, indica, hybrid and sativa labels barely matched the mix of terpenes, the compounds behind weed's smell. Strain names did a bit better.
cl_can_strain_labels.but: The labels came from a strain website, not the bags. And nobody measured how the weed made people feel.
how: Researchers used lab results for about 90,000 flower samples from licensed growers in six US states, 2013 to 2021. In every state, 94 to 97 in 100 samples had at least five times as much THC as CBD. Labels came from a strain website, matched by name, and weren't compared on THC or CBD.

In 41,201 samples where THC outweighed CBD, the three labels were all mixed up in their terpenes. Sativa was twice as common in one smell type, rich in terpinolene, but most of those were still hybrid.
Strain names did better: for 26 of 41 widely grown names, different growers' products were more alike than chance. For 13 they weren't, and two, LSD and Durban Poison, were less alike.
A small Dutch study tested two coffee-shop strains, one sativa-type and one indica-type. They had similar THC but different terpenes, and each varied a lot from bag to bag.
cl_can_strain_labels.rate: One very large set of lab records, but it checked only smell compounds, used a strain website's labels instead of the packages, and measured no effects on people.

cl_opi_treatment_mortality.q: Is it dangerous to stop methadone or buprenorphine (Suboxone)?
cl_opi_treatment_mortality.short: Deaths were more common off treatment, most of all in the first 4 weeks after leaving. In 16 methadone studies, about 36 in 1,000 died a year off treatment, against 11 on it.
cl_opi_treatment_mortality.but: The main figures lump together everyone who left, for any reason. People who leave differ in other ways. So the studies can't show that stopping itself caused the deaths.
how: In 16 groups of people on methadone, about 11 in 1,000 died each year in treatment, against about 36 out of it. Every group had more deaths out of treatment, though in the biggest recent groups the gap was smaller: about 6 or 7 a year, against 12 to 18.

5 recent studies, with lower death rates overall, split deaths by time: about 32 a year per 1,000 people in the first 4 weeks off methadone, against about 14 later on. The first 4 weeks on it looked riskier too, but that could be chance.

With buprenorphine, almost all the deaths came from Australian studies. Deaths were also higher in the first 4 weeks off, about 32 against 11 a year per 1,000, but that's from just two studies. Counting overdoses alone, 3 methadone studies found no clear rise in those weeks, but only 20 happened then.

Did finishing treatment matter? Only 3 studies looked, and the review doesn't say what finishing meant. In two small ones, deaths after leaving ran 3 to 4 times higher when treatment wasn't finished (about 69 against 17, and 84 against 26 a year per 1,000). The third, which counted only the first 4 weeks, found no clear difference.
cl_opi_treatment_mortality.rate: Sixteen studies in several countries all found more deaths off treatment, but we saw them only through one weak review. Nobody chose at random who stayed, and people who leave may differ, so how much stopping matters is unknown.

cl_opi_withdrawal_deaths.q: Can opioid withdrawal itself kill you?
cl_opi_withdrawal_deaths.short: Deaths have been reported, but nobody knows how often. One editorial lists 11, all in jail. It suggests vomiting and diarrhoea, left untreated, can dry the body out until the heart fails.
cl_opi_withdrawal_deaths.but: It's one editorial's short list, from the news, a court case and a prosecutor's letter. It has no medical details. And nobody counted how many went through withdrawal, so there's no rate.
how: The authors' idea: vomiting and diarrhoea that don't stop, left untreated, dry the body out. Blood sodium rises, and the heart can fail.

The cases: a woman in custody in the UK in 1998, and 10 people in US jails from 2013 to 2016, aged 18 to 49. For those 10, the list gives only the year, sex, age, place and a news source (for one, a prosecutor's letter).
The authors say each death came slowly, with time to treat it, and call the deaths neglect or a lack of medical care. Their list gives no medical details to check this.
They say such deaths are rising but give no counts over time. Nothing here covers withdrawal outside custody.
cl_opi_withdrawal_deaths.rate: One editorial, using cases from news reports, a court case and a prosecutor's letter, all in custody, with no medical details. Nobody counted how many people went through withdrawal, so how often it kills is unknown.

interactions.statement: Taking MDMA with LSD pushes heart rate and blood pressure higher than LSD alone.
interactions.why: In a lab study of 24 people, they rose about as high as on MDMA alone. Body temperature wasn't clearly higher.

heroin.statement: Death rates were about the same in and out of methadone treatment.
heroin.why: In 16 groups of people on methadone, about 11 in 1,000 died each year in treatment, against about 36 out of it. People who leave differ in other ways, so this can't show cause.

heroin.statement: You can't die from opioid withdrawal.
heroin.why: Deaths have been reported, all in jail; one editorial suggests untreated vomiting and diarrhoea can dry the body out. How often it happens is unknown.

psilocybin.statement: Given LSD or the drug in magic mushrooms without being told which, most people can't tell which one it was.
psilocybin.why: In a 28-person lab study, people named the right drug after 71 to 86 in 100 sessions, though they rated the trips alike on most measures.

lsd.statement: Adding MDMA to LSD has been shown to make a bad trip less likely.
lsd.why: In a lab study of 24 people in a calm hospital room, bad-feeling and fear scores weren't clearly lower than on LSD alone.

lsd.statement: In a lab test, people rated trips on LSD and on psilocybin, the drug in magic mushrooms, as much alike.
lsd.why: In 28 people, the ratings barely differed. But that's no proof they're the same, and most could tell which drug they'd had.

cannabis.statement: Indica and sativa labels tell you which smell compounds your weed has.
cannabis.why: In 41,201 US lab-tested samples, the labels barely matched the mix of smell compounds (terpenes). The labels came from a strain website, not the bags, and effects weren't measured.

cannabis.statement: Almost all weed tested from licensed growers in six US states was THC-rich, not CBD-rich.
cannabis.why: In six US states, 94 to 97 in 100 lab-tested flower samples from licensed growers had at least five times as much THC as CBD.

methadone-buprenorphine.statement: In studies, death rates were highest in the first weeks after leaving methadone.
methadone-buprenorphine.why: In 5 studies, deaths in the first 4 weeks off methadone ran at about 32 a year per 1,000 people, against about 14 later on. People who leave may differ in other ways.
